caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 143 of 1987
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Ozair Farooq Senior Advocate with Sheikh Mohammad Morshed, Mr. Md. Shakhawat Hossain Advocate ------ for the appellant.
Mr. Asad Hossain Chowdhury, Advocate ------ for the respondents.
parties:
M/s. Bangladesh Tennery and another
Vs.
Janata Bank
full_judgment: 2. The facts loading to the filing of the suit in short is that on the prayer made on behalf of M/S. Bangladesh Tannery, a firm, the defendant No. 1 the plaintiff Janata Bank, opened a letter of credit to import caustic soda from abroad, On receipt of the shipping document the plaintiff informed the defendants to retire the documents but they failed to do so, instead, on their prayer the plaintiff arranged release of the imported goods on payment of duties and taxes by creating a loan against the imported merchandise being LIM account no. 24/5189/76 and stored in their godown at Dhaka. Thereafter the defendants, inspite of repeated letters and notices, failed to take delivery of the imported chemicals on payment of the dues of the bank. As such the plaintiff bank was constrained to sell 251 bags of imported caustic Soda at Tk. 91,500/- an credited the said amount to the account of the plaintiff and brought the suit for recovery of the rest Tk. 4, 02,420/- as on 25.11.1981. The defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that since the defendant firm was declared abandoned in 1972, the suit is not maintainable, that the suit is misconceived barred by limitation etc. The further case of the defendants is that the bank purposely delayed disposal of the goods in-spite of their repented prayers, thereafter, sold the goods at an unconscionably low price of only. Tk.  91,500/- customer for obtaining a comparatively better value for these goods for which they suffered less because even on sale by negotiation the imported chemicals fetched uncontainable low price. He further submits that had these goods been sold for proper value and in time, the dues of the bank would have been fully adjusted. As such he prays for dismissal of the suit because of the latches on the part of the officials of the bank in not selling the goods at a proper time and at a proper price. On the other hand Mr. Asad Hossain Chowdhury, Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that since the claim of the bank is admitted as regards creation of the LIM account and payment against letter of credit as well as towards customs dues and other taxes and so long it is also not denied that the defendants, failed to take delivery of the goods stored in their godown, they are liable to pay the entire claim with interest. As regards the lower selling value of the stored chemicals he submits that the goods were imported as far as back in 1976, as such the quality of these chemicals deteriorated and did not fetch the desired price in the open market but without any fault on the part of the officials of the bank rather this was due to the failure on the part of defendants to take delivery of the goods on payment to the bank. In that view of the matter, the learned Advocate prays for dismissal of the appeal.
